topics.label: Welcome and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer biology lecture series, the interdisciplinary student audience, and the core learning outcomes of the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Normal Differentiation and Genetic Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the fundamental nature of cancer as a breakdown of developmental differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Distinctions, Progression, and Nomenclature of Benign and Malignant Tumours
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the diagnostic criteria, histological progression, and standardized nomenclature used to differentiate benign from malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer-Induced Disease and Death
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the physiological and anatomical mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors impair organ function and cause patient mortality.

topics.label: Tumour Incidence Across Human Populations and Animal Species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the epidemiology, frequency, and tissue distribution of tumors across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Practice of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical rationale, methodologies, and relative effectiveness of screening programs for early cancer detection across different organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Briefing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by referencing the learning outcomes and outlining expectations for upcoming practicals and lectures.
